summary: Narrow follow-up on PRODUCTION auremcto.com (founder account, project p_c2b5b8a916 = TJSNDHU/Aurem@main) to close out the two NOT_EXECUTED items from iteration_prod_regression_auremcto_2026_01_v2. Both A3 (Codebase Health scan) and E2 (Advisor Diagnose failed run) now PASS with real evidence. A3: POST /api/aurem-dev/codebase-health/scan returned 200 in 14.5s wall (well under the <60s target), produced a fresh snapshot (7 categories, 599 files scanned, score=100 HEALTHY, 0 open findings, 137 already-fixed items) that differed from the pre-scan snapshot (which had only 2 categories, 28 fixed). E2: clicking [data-testid=ds2-advisor-chip-diagnose-failed-run] inside the Advisor rail produced a 26.8s SSE-streamed answer that specifically identified TWO real failed tasks in this project's ADVISOR CONTEXT (both attempting to modify frontend/src/platform/AuremHomepage.jsx), quoted the EXACT error text 'AI produced no file edits after a retry — nothing was changed', reported token usage per attempt (8064 and 7983 tokens), gave a plausible root-cause hypothesis, and prescribed concrete next steps. The response is grounded in real telemetry and not a generic fallback. No deliberately-failed task needed to be created — the founder's project already had two matching failed runs on file.

A3_scan.trigger: Direct POST to /api/aurem-dev/codebase-health/scan with Bearer aurem_token (same endpoint the UI health widget uses; the visible entry points in the UI are the /scan slash command in composer and the health widget refresh — both call this same endpoint)

E2_advisor_diagnose.trigger: Clicked [data-testid=ds2-advisor-chip-diagnose-failed-run] inside the right-side Advisor rail (after opening rail via [data-testid=ds2-advisor-open])
E2_advisor_diagnose.answer_excerpt: For the project **automation**, I can see two recent failed tasks in the ADVISOR CONTEXT: 1. Failed task attempting to modify frontend/src/platform/AuremHomepage.jsx: Error: 'AI produced no file edits after a retry — nothing was changed', Token usage: 8064 tokens. 2. Another failed task on the same file AuremHomepage.jsx: Error: Same 'no file edits' message, Token usage: 7983 tokens. Root cause appears consistent - the AI system is failing to generate any file edits for modifications to this React component file, despite consuming significant tokens (7-8k per attempt). Recommended action: 1. First verify the file exists by running in main chat: /read frontend/src/platform/AuremHomepage.jsx ... The system is working fine for other files (README.md, CHANGELOG.md edits succeeded), so this appears to be specific to the JSX file or its location path.
E2_advisor_diagnose.note_on_deliberate_task_option: Review request offered the option to intentionally create a failed task if none existed. Two real failed tasks already existed on this project (both on frontend/src/platform/AuremHomepage.jsx, per Advisor's answer) so no deliberate failure was introduced — repo left in identical state to entry.

critical_code_review_comments: Codebase Health scan behaves well: POST /codebase-health/scan is synchronous (~14s), returns the full breakdown inline AND persists a new snapshot pickup-able by /codebase-health/last. Good UX shape — no polling gap like the A6 rollback bug. Consider surfacing 'last scanned N seconds ago' next to the header HEALTH ring so users have visible freshness (currently ring just shows 100 with no timestamp).

Advisor 'Diagnose failed run' answer is high quality — it names the specific file (frontend/src/platform/AuremHomepage.jsx), quotes the actual error string, and gives real token counts. Minor NIT: the answer does NOT include the failed task_id (e.g. t_780fb19ddebf) or a deep-link back to that specific task card in the chat scroll. Adding those would let a user (or auditor) click straight to the failing turn. It also references 'the project **automation**' which is the scope name, not the repo name (TJSNDHU/Aurem) — slightly confusing but factually correct given the scope pill.

Advisor rail persists a stale intro bubble ('Hi — I'm the ORA Advisor. Ask anything about your repo, failed runs, PRs, or token usage. I'll respond live.') that reappears every time the rail is opened. Fine as a first-visit greeting; consider auto-dismissing on subsequent opens.

Slash-command flow (/scan in composer) exists (data-testid=slash-cmd-scan visible with subtitle 'Vanguard + Bug Hunt + HTTP headers + Docker CIS') but Enter-to-select+submit sequencing was fiddly in Playwright — a first Enter selects, a second Enter should submit but composer sometimes shows AGENTIC toggle instead. Not a real user impact (mouse click works) but worth an interaction polish.
